gui.neroeconomy.handbook.chapter.auto_tr: An auto-trade rule buys or sells for you while you are away. Set the item or a tag, the price each, how many per day and a total. A rule never goes past them.
A buy rule holds its budget and a sell rule holds its goods, so it can always pay or deliver. Pause one rule, or all of them at once, from My orders.
The Auto-Trader block runs a rule from its own slots, so hoppers and pipes can feed it. It never keeps a chunk loaded: when its chunk unloads, its rule pauses and says so.
gui.neroeconomy.handbook.chapter.credits: Credits are the money of this server. Your balance is kept by the server, not in an item, so you cannot drop it or lose it when you die.
New players get some starting credits. For your first minutes of play they stay locked: you can spend them on fees, the Merchant Houses and the exchange, but not give them to other players.
Credits from your sales wait in the Wallet tab until you press Collect. To pay a player, type their name and how much. Pay asks twice, so nothing is sent by mistake.
A Credit Chip used on a Bank Terminal turns into credits. Each chip you use in one day is worth a little less than the one before.
gui.neroeconomy.handbook.chapter.data.1: The server keeps only what the economy needs: your balance, your own activity, your vault, orders, shops and investments, and whether you were given this book.
gui.neroeconomy.handbook.chapter.data.2: Your activity log can be turned off in the Wallet tab. Other players never see your name in their activity, and you never see theirs.
gui.neroeconomy.handbook.chapter.data.3: You can ask an admin to export everything kept about you, or to erase it. Erasing removes your account here, with its credits and goods.
gui.neroeconomy.handbook.chapter.data.4: No IP address is ever kept. Questions about your data: info@neroland.co.za
gui.neroeconomy.handbook.chapter.fair_pl: Fees are small and go to the server's Reserve, which pays for jobs, the Houses and interest. A fee is worked out on the whole order, so splitting an order never pays less.
Limits stop anyone draining the economy: daily caps on the Houses, auto-trade and Credit Chips, limits on what you can invest, and a daily cap on spending from the app.
Everything that moves credits or goods asks twice and says what you give and get. Nothing done in creative mode can add value to the real economy.
Merchant Houses are traders run by the server. They sell from stock that refills slowly, and buy with the credits they have. Each one deals in its own goods.
Selling to a House lowers what it pays for that item; buying from it raises its price. Both drift back over time. A House also has daily limits, in total and for each player.
Reference prices follow what players pay each other, slowly and within limits, so one big trade cannot swing a price.
gui.neroeconomy.handbook.chapter.investi: The exchange lists made-up companies, an index fund and savings bonds. You buy from and sell to the exchange itself, at its price, plus a small fee.
Share prices move up and down. Steady shares move a little and pay dividends; risky shares move a lot either way. The index fund holds a little of every company.
A savings bond locks credits for a set time and pays interest. It cannot lose. Cash it in early and you get back only what you put in.

The risks: a share can be worth less when you sell than when you bought. Buying and selling straight away always loses. You must hold a share a while before selling, and how much you can hold is limited.
Practice mode lets you try all of this with play credits that never touch your real balance. A banner stays up while it is on.
gui.neroeconomy.handbook.chapter.jobs.1: Jobs ask for goods: contracts, deliveries and bounties. Claim one, gather what it wants, then hand it in for the payout. Who posted a job is not shown.
gui.neroeconomy.handbook.chapter.jobs.2: To post a job of your own, say what you want, how many and the payout. The payout is held until the job ends, and comes back if nobody does it.
gui.neroeconomy.handbook.chapter.jobs.3: An auction sells to the highest bid. Your bid is held while it stands and comes back if someone bids more. A late bid can add a little time, so nobody snatches a lot at the last second.
gui.neroeconomy.handbook.chapter.jobs.4: Start an auction with what is in your hand: how many, the least bid you accept and how long it runs. A fee is taken from the winning bid.
The Market tab lists what is for sale: other players' goods, shops and the Merchant Houses. Search for an item, pick a row and type how many you want.
Quote shows the total, the fee and whether the goods go to your inventory or your vault. Nothing is bought yet. Press Buy once to read what you pay and get, and again to buy.
Sell puts goods from your hand or your vault up for sale at your price. A small fee is paid to list them. When they sell, the credits less the market fee wait in your Wallet.
Buying and selling on the Market
A buy order says: I will pay this much each for this many. Use Want on the Market tab. Your credits are held while it waits, so the seller is sure to be paid.

Orders match on their own: best price first, then the oldest. An order can fill a bit at a time. If you offered more than the price it filled at, you get the difference back. You never trade with yourself.
Goods from a buy order go to your vault. My orders lists everything you have open, and cancelling an order gives back what was held for it.
gui.neroeconomy.handbook.chapter.shops.1: A Player Shop is a block you place and stock with one kind of item, at a price you set. Other players buy from it in person, and it is listed on the Market too.
gui.neroeconomy.handbook.chapter.shops.2: The Shop tab lists your shops with their stock and price. Pick one to change its price: the first press shows the old and new price, the second sets it.
gui.neroeconomy.handbook.chapter.shops.3: A shop nobody uses for a long time closes on its own, and its stock goes to your vault. A shop shown in yellow will close soon.
gui.neroeconomy.handbook.chapter.trading: To trade face to face, sneak and use an empty hand on a player, or pick them in Trade nearby. A window opens where each of you puts in items and credits.
Any change on either side clears both confirms. When both of you confirm, the trade waits three seconds, then swaps at once. Walking away or leaving the game gives everything back.
An offer is a trade by post: send items and credits to a player by name, and ask for something back. What you send is held until they accept or decline, or the offer runs out.
The player you send an offer to sees it as coming from "a player": an offer never names who sent it, and the offers sent to you never name their senders either.
gui.neroeconomy.handbook.chapter.vault.1: Your vault is a safe store for goods, kept by the server. Things you buy with no room in your inventory, refunds, and goods from orders that filled while you were away all land there.
gui.neroeconomy.handbook.chapter.vault.2: Move items in and out at a Bank Terminal. The vault holds a set number of stacks. When it is full you cannot buy more into it, but refunds still arrive, so nothing is ever lost.
gui.neroeconomy.handbook.chapter.vault.3: A stack marked (changed) is not a plain item: it may be enchanted, damaged or renamed. It only stacks with exact copies of itself.

stock.neroeconomy.bloomspice_traders.des: Deals in cocoa, sugar, honey and rare foods. Tastes change fast, and so does its price.
stock.neroeconomy.deepcore_mining.descri: Digs iron, copper and coal. Slow and dependable, and pays a dividend.
stock.neroeconomy.ductway_freight.descri: Moves goods by rail, hopper and boat. Earns a little on everything that travels.
stock.neroeconomy.farside_salvage.descri: Recovers meteor metal and void crystal from beyond the sky. Big wins, big losses.
stock.neroeconomy.glimmerstone_prospecti: Hunts for diamonds, emeralds and gold. A rich find sends it soaring; a dry spell sinks it.
stock.neroeconomy.greenfield_farms.descr: Grows wheat and other everyday crops. Calm, with a regular dividend.
stock.neroeconomy.index.description: A share of everything: it moves by the average of every listed company, so it is less bumpy than any single one.
stock.neroeconomy.kindlewick_power.descr: Keeps furnaces and generators burning. Steady demand, steady price, and a dividend.
stock.neroeconomy.lanternleaf_decor.desc: Makes glass, dyes, lanterns and furnishings. Small and calm, with a regular dividend.
stock.neroeconomy.redpulse_dynamics.desc: Builds redstone machinery. Clever, unproven, and prone to large swings.
stock.neroeconomy.settlers_row_supply.de: Sells timber, stone and beds to new colonies. Grows as settlements grow.
stock.neroeconomy.skylantern_launchworks: Builds rockets. The most expensive share on the exchange, and the wildest.
